clauses.current_legal_basis: Executive Order 13827 of March 19, 2018 (83 FR 12469) took additional steps under the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692 of March 8, 2015, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. That emergency was continued by notice every year from 2019 through 2026; the held Notice of February 18, 2026 (91 FR 8357, FR Doc. 2026-03502) continues it for one year and names Executive Order 13827 among the orders that took additional steps under it. The held Federal Register texts of every executive order numbered 13828 through 14435 (14435 was signed 2026-10-05) were scanned for this order's number; the only order that cites it with a changing verb is Executive Order 13857, which amended subsection (d) of section 3 (listed as a later event on that clause). Orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are not held and are covered only by the catalog search. Executive Order 14373 of January 9, 2026 (91 FR 2045) declares a separate national emergency about Foreign Government Deposit Funds and supersedes earlier executive orders only to the extent they block, regulate or otherwise affect those funds; it does not name this order, and no clause of this order addresses funds held by the United States Treasury on behalf of the Government of Venezuela, so it is not treated as ending any clause. The Federal Register executive-order catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog, checked 2026-11-25) shows only Executive Order 13857's amendment of subsection (d) of section 3, and the eCFR search (current-law:ecfr) shows regulations implementing the order. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1(a) prohibits United States persons and persons within the United States from transactions in, financing for, and other dealings in any digital currency, digital coin or digital token issued by, for or on behalf of the Government of Venezuela on or after January 9, 2018. The January 9, 2018 date fixes which instruments are covered and does not make the prohibition expire. No held instrument revokes or narrows it. This clause depends on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692; the yearly continuation notices are recorded as later events on section 1 of this order and are not ends.

clauses.reason: Section 3(d) defines the Government of Venezuela, which fixes the reach of the prohibition in section 1. Executive Order 13857 of January 25, 2019 (84 FR 509), section 1(a), amended subsection (d) of section 3 to read as follows: the term Government of Venezuela includes the state and Government of Venezuela, any political subdivision, agency or instrumentality (including the Central Bank of Venezuela and Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A.), any person owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by them, and any person who has acted or purported to act for or on behalf of any of them, including as a member of the Maduro regime. Before the amendment the definition covered the Government of Venezuela, its subdivisions, agencies and instrumentalities (including the Central Bank and PdVSA) and any person owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of, the Government of Venezuela. The amended definition is broader, so the substance changed. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert and restated provisions, the clause continues, amended, until its parent order ends; this order has not ended. Reviewer note: the current wording of this definition is the 2019 wording, not the wording printed in the original order. The prohibition it defines continues.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13827 (83 FR 12469, signed 2018-03-19, published 2018-03-21, FR Doc. 2018-05916) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13827.txt, the registered official original. Number, date, title and signature date match the register. The 13-clause inventory (section 1(a) and (b), section 2(a) and (b), section 3 with paragraphs (a) through (d), sections 4 through 7) covers the whole text. The order is emergency-dependent: it rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692, which the President continued by notice each year from 2019 through 2026 (eight held notices recorded as later events on section 1; the last, signed February 18, 2026, runs to March 2027, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14). Only one later instrument amends the order: Executive Order 13857 (2019-01-25) amended the definition in section 3(d), recorded as a later event with the before and after substance. No instrument revokes or supersedes the order or any other clause. Executive Order 13835, Executive Order 13850 and Executive Order 13857 cite it as an earlier step without revoking it. The held corpus of executive-order texts runs through Executive Order 14435 (signed 2026-10-05); orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are covered only by the catalog search. The held Federal Register texts of every executive order numbered 13828 through 14435 (14435 was signed 2026-10-05) were scanned for this order's number; the only order that cites it with a changing verb is Executive Order 13857, which amended subsection (d) of section 3 (listed as a later event on that clause). Orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are not held and are covered only by the catalog search. Executive Order 14373 of January 9, 2026 (91 FR 2045) declares a separate national emergency about Foreign Government Deposit Funds and supersedes earlier executive orders only to the extent they block, regulate or otherwise affect those funds; it does not name this order, and no clause of this order addresses funds held by the United States Treasury on behalf of the Government of Venezuela, so it is not treated as ending any clause.

savings.reason: Executive Order 13827 has no savings or transition clause: section 1(b) preserves the prohibition notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits, and section 6 only disclaims private rights. The amendment by Executive Order 13857 changes the definition in section 3(d) without saving or transferring any right or action from the original wording, and the bounded searches found no instrument that would do so.
